thread:
devin: FYI — seen a big spike in GPU pod evictions in us-west2 this morning, looks like NIC saturation + latebind is the combo. small-slot jobs get preempted in waves.

kai: Can you paste the node stats? which NIC (eg en0/en1) and driver?

devin: Throwing the short dump: 
```
node/usw2-rack12-n03: rx-drop=3124 tx-qlen=1274, net_backlog=2048, nvlink=ok
kubelet: podEvictedReason=Preempted, evictSource=kube-scheduler, taints: gpu_reserved=true:NoSchedule
scheduler: latebind=true, preferCompact=true, preemptWindows=60s
```

anita: Hmm. net_backlog at 2048 is worrying for multi-GPU host. Are we hitting host egress limits on that AZ?

maria: Traffic graphs show egress peaking ~2.8Gbps on that node group between 03:12-03:24 UTC. Most pods are embedding batches hitting remote store.

ops-lead: @sre-bot can you confirm if any host-level egress policy changed around 03:00 UTC?

sre-bot: deploy-audit: no network-policy changes, but autoscaler bumped 6 instances into the warm-pool at 02:58 UTC.

kai: Autoscaler bump might have pushed compact packing into a different placement pattern. If many small pods co-locate on a host with one outbound link, their combined egress + IPVS can saturate NIC. That triggers kube-proxy latencies -> deeper scheduling churn.

devin: We also saw a weird interaction with soft-taints we rolled out last week: nodes get tainted gpu_reserved=true:PreferNoSchedule when warm pool is used. Latebind then tries to backfill which causes preemption of tiny pods.

maria: Outcomes: 1) eviction waves for tiny pod classes (batch size <= 4), 2) job restarts -> increased token spend, 3) customer-facing higher tail latency.

anita: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle egress on those nodes via tc (short term) 2) change scheduler predicate to consider node egress usage 3) adjust latebind window to higher latency for us-west2. Thoughts?

kai: Agree. Also consider soft-affinity weights: avoid strict compacting of small-slot pods on same host. Slightly prefer spreading when net_backlog > threshold.

devin: I can push a targeted tc rule to the two worst nodes for now. Who wants to own longer-term?

ops-lead: Maria + Kai to own follow-up. Devin please patch the tc and post results. I’ll open an incident PM for exec visibility.

maria: On it. I'll add a quick scheduler tweak flag experiment: `--egress-aware=true` behind rollout. Start with canary in us-west2c with 10% of traffic.

kai: We'll need tests: synthetic tiny-pod packing that simulates embedding traffic. I have a script; will share.

devin: tc applied to rack12-n03 and rack12-n07 at 03:40 UTC: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 1.5gbit burst 32k latency 50ms`

maria: After tc, evictions dropped by ~70% in those nodes, job tail latency improved ~32%. Still want the scheduler change though.

anita: Cost note: spreading small pods may increase instance footprint ~8% compared to tight packing, but that beats customer-facing retries and token cost. Put cost estimate in doc.

ops-lead: Good tradeoff. Maria/Kai file RFC for egress-aware scheduling + soft-affinity tuning. Include cost vs reliability numbers and rollout plan.

devin: Logging follow-up: captured kube-scheduler traces in the window and saved to s3://redwood-ops/sched-traces/1712349999.tar.gz

maria: RFC draft by EOD. Kai will post synthetic test results.

kai: test script: `scripts/net-simulate --pods 120 --gpus 0.25 --egress 300mbps` — will run against canary cluster and post charts.

anita: Also add a runbook: if NIC backlog > 1500 and eviction rate > 5/min then preempt new latebind placements for that AZ and redirect to fallback region.

devin: thanks all. I'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
